label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the weekly branch always does `next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7)` regardless of whether the run hour on the current day has already passed, unlike the daily branch which only advances a day `if (next <= from)`. So a weekly schedule created before 06:00 UTC on its target day (e.g. Monday 05:40 UTC) skips that day's run entirely and waits a full week for the first email, matching both reports (created 09:00 in August worked by luck since that's after the run hour; created 05:40 in October missed the same-day run). A PR mirroring the daily logic for weekly (only add 7 days when `next <= from`) has been opened to fix this.

input.title: Fix weekly export schedules skipping their first run
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the "weekly" branch always adds 7 days to `next` (today at RUN_HOUR_UTC), unlike the "daily" branch, which only advances the date when `next <= from`. This means a weekly schedule created before RUN_HOUR_UTC on its chosen day always skips that day's run and first fires a week later, matching the reported behaviour (a schedule created at 05:40 UTC, before the 06:00 UTC run hour, sent nothing until the following Monday).

Proposed fix: make the "weekly" case mirror "daily" by only bumping `next` forward by 7 days when `next <= from`; otherwise leave `next` as the same-day RUN_HOUR_UTC time so the first run happens on the day the schedule was created, provided that time hasn't already passed.
